This was written by Maurice Williams with both melody and doo-wop accompaniment strongly emphasizing the clave rhythm. It was first recorded by Excello Records in January 1957 and quickly released as a rhythm-and-blues song by Williams' R&B group, The Gladiolas. The song is noted for its spoken recitation by the lead singer ("My Darlin' I need you..."). The Gladiolas, featuring Williams, were from Lancaster, South Carolina, where they had been together since high school. Their original version of the song was on the small Excello label. (Excello primarily recording "swamp blues" songs in Crowley, Louisiana.)

The Diamonds' version followed a month later. The Diamonds were soon covering Little Darlin' successfully. The Diamonds were a Canadian pop group that evolved into a Doo-Wop group. The Diamonds' version reached number two in sales for eight weeks on the Billboard Hot 100. Billboard ranked this version as the No. 3 song for 1957.

The Diamonds' version is generally considered a superior version. Allmusic critic Stephen Thomas Erlewine argues that the Diamonds Little Darlin' is an unusual example of a cover being better than the original:

"The Diamonds' take remained the bigger hit, and over the years, the better-known version. Normally, this would have been an outrage, but there's a reason why the Diamonds' version has sustained its popularity over the years: it's a better, fiercer recording. Both versions are good, even if they're a little silly, because it's a good doo wop song, giving each member of the quartet a lot to do. At times, the vocal phrases verge on self-parody -- the "ai-ya-yi-yai-yai-ya"'s or the "wella-wella"'s -- which may be why The Diamonds' version is superior."

This stuff works best for me (weight and protection wise) to carry at work but if people want to go IV or go with another brands 3+ totally do it - but I have yet to see this armor fail its rating

I mean, if you want to go for 3+ then go ahead but I know for a fact that AR500 has put out bad batches of armor before. I also know that AT Armor had at one point a program in place to trade in older, crappier AR500 plates for some good stuff. Personally, I'll run ceramic Lvl 4 stuff like I had in the Army. Some of this new UHMWP stuff thats coming out is supposed to be extremely good, but very expensive. I'm not going to risk life, limb on a gambler $150 plate though.

Scorpion Tactical supposedly cuts theirs different than AR500 (doesn't compromise heat treat on the edges which is the only bad batches I've heard of from AR500 by the edges being compromised) They both have their certificates and from what I've heard ceramic can be compromised from a drop which could easily happen with what Im doing with it/need something thats not as bulky. To each there own but I don't believe this is a gamble/can't find anything backing that up (not arguing lvl 4 is a higher rating, just that this 3+ will do what I need it to at a lighter weight)

Ceramic can be compromised from a drop, but it isn't likely. I used to throw my IOTV around all of the time when we got back from training/missions/whatever and I never broke my plates.

What I will say is that lvl 3+ will still probably not be enough for dealing with a domestic fight because you have no idea what caliber the enemy will be using.

Pay the extra 75 per plate and get lvl4 ceramic.

Dont cheap out on your ventilation insurance
Totally understand why people would go with that but weight and bulkiness should also be considered depending on what your going to do with it
